stories.head: Anthropic ships claude-opus-5 to the API — same release adds tool_change event streaming
stories.brief: SDK 0.120.0 adds the claude-opus-5 model plus tool add/remove streaming blocks.
stories.tldr: Anthropic’s Python SDK release 0.120.0, dated 2026-07-24, adds the claude-opus-5 model to the API [1]. The same commit adds tool addition/removal blocks and tool_change events [1].
stories.why: You build AI agents on Claude, so both halves land directly in your stack: a new top-end model to route hard steps to, and tool_change streaming that lets a long-running agent’s toolset shift mid-session instead of being fixed at request time.

sources.claim: Anthropic added claude-opus-5 to its production API on July 24, 2026, alongside new tool-change event streaming for agentic workflows.
sources.excerpt:
## 0.120.0 (2026-07-24)

### Features

* **api:** add claude-opus-5 model ([bf4e31c](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/commit/bf4e31c17c43ba2b409bec57e1856b025d159f1a))
* **api:** add tool addition/removal blocks and tool_change events ([bf4e31c](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/commit/bf4e31c17c43ba2b409bec57e1816b025d159f1a))
sources.summary: Anthropic official Python SDK changelog v0.120.0. The entry confirms claude-opus-5 API availability on July 24. Same commit also adds tool_change events (tool addition/removal streaming), a capability relevant to long-horizon agentic tasks. Primary source: Anthropic’s own GitHub org (anthropics).
sources.trustReason: Official Anthropic SDK changelog in the anthropics GitHub org; excerpt contains verbatim changelog bullets with commit hashes directly substantiating both the claude-opus-5 addition and tool_change event streaming; no hedging, named origin, specific date and version.

stories.head: Gemini 3.6 Flash goes stronger and cheaper than 3.5 Flash — 3.5 Flash-Lite takes the throughput floor
stories.brief: Google’s 3.6 Flash cuts tokens and price; 3.5 Flash-Lite anchors the cheap tier.
stories.tldr: Google’s official Gemini API cookbook describes Gemini 3.6 Flash as stronger on complex agentic and multimodal tasks while reducing token usage, at a lower price point than 3.5 Flash [1]. Beside it, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite is positioned as the fastest, lowest-cost model in the 3.5 family, outperforming prior Flash-Lite generations for high-throughput execution [2].
stories.why: As an engineer running agent workloads, a model that claims better agentic performance on fewer tokens at a lower price changes your cost-per-run maths — worth benchmarking against your current Claude routing before you commit to a per-step model mix.

sources.claim: Google launched Gemini 3.6 Flash on July 21, 2026, with stronger agentic and multimodal performance and lower token usage than Gemini 3.5 Flash at a reduced price.
sources.excerpt: **Gemini 3.6 Flash**: Stronger performance on complex agentic and multimodal tasks while reducing token usage, at a lower price point than 3.5 Flash. Learn how to build with the model in the [Getting started cookbook](./quickstarts/Get_started.ipynb)
sources.summary: Google official Gemini API Cookbook README (google-gemini GitHub org), updated to highlight Gemini 3.6 Flash launch. Search results corroborate July 21 date and $1.50/$7.50 per 1M token pricing.
sources.trustReason: Official google-gemini GitHub org (Google’s primary developer documentation for Gemini); excerpt directly substantiates the agentic/multimodal performance, reduced token usage, and lower price positioning vs. 3.5 Flash; minor gap is that the July 21 date is from the row’s time field rather than the excerpt text itself, but the source authority and content match are strong.

sources.claim: Google co-launched Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite on July 21, 2026, positioning it as the fastest and lowest-cost model in the 3.5 family, outperforming prior Flash-Lite generations.
sources.excerpt: **Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite**: The fastest, lowest-cost model in the 3.5 family. Outperforms prior Flash-Lite generations for high-throughput execution.
sources.summary: Same source document as the Gemini 3.6 Flash row. Google co-announced Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite in the same July 21 launch alongside Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber.
sources.trustReason: Same official google-gemini GitHub org README as the 3.6 Flash row; excerpt states ‘fastest, lowest-cost model in the 3.5 family’ and ‘outperforms prior Flash-Lite generations’ verbatim, directly substantiating the claim.

stories.head: Unity simulates, Unreal renders — live PolySpatial demo syncs physics, lighting and input across engines
stories.brief: Fantasy Kingdom runs in Unity while Unreal draws it live over a PolySpatial link.
stories.tldr: A live demo showed the Fantasy Kingdom sample simulated in Unity and rendered in real time by Unreal, with physics, lighting, and input synchronized between the engines [1]. The bridge is a client-server protocol called PolySpatial, which also supports multiplayer as a first-class feature [1].
stories.why: For your UE5 work this reframes Unreal as a renderer that can be fed by an external simulation — worth watching how a client-server sync layer interacts with Nanite and your Unreal Insights frame budgets before it reaches your pipeline.

sources.claim: At the Unite Seoul 2026 keynote Unity showed—for the first time publicly—a live cross-engine demo of the Fantasy Kingdom sample simulated in Unity and rendered in Unreal Engine via a client-server protocol called PolySpatial, with physics, lighting and input synchronized in real time.
sources.excerpt: A live demo showed the Fantasy Kingdom sample simulated in Unity and rendered in real-time by Unreal, with physics, lighting, and input synchronized between engines via a client-server protocol called PolySpatial, which also supports multiplayer as a first-class feature.
sources.summary: Unity blog recap of the Unite Seoul 2026 keynote. Page is proxy-blocked; excerpt reproduced consistently across multiple search result snippets.
sources.trustReason: Official Unity Technologies blog; excerpt is highly specific and maps directly onto every named element of the claim.

stories.head: Unity 7 announced — pitched at creators, cross-functional teams and coding agents working together
stories.brief: Unity aims version 7 at coding agents collaborating with humans through the dev cycle.
stories.tldr: Unity 7 has been announced, described as designed for “a faster-moving, more open industry where creators, cross-functional teams, and coding agents can seamlessly collaborate across every stage of the development cycle” [1].
stories.why: You sit on both sides of this: an engine vendor building for coding agents is a direct signal for how the AI agents you develop on Claude might plug into a game-dev toolchain rather than sit beside it.

sources.claim: 80.lv reports Unity 7 is designed for AI-agent collaboration with no breaking changes from Unity 6, targeting a ‘faster-moving, more open industry’ where human and coding-agent teams collaborate across the full dev lifecycle.
sources.excerpt: Unity 7 is designed for “a faster-moving, more open industry where creators, cross-functional teams, and coding agents can seamlessly collaborate across every stage of the development cycle.”
sources.summary: 80.lv editorial coverage of the Unity 7 announcement from Unite Seoul, published July 22 2026. Page is proxy-blocked; excerpt sourced from search snippet.
sources.trustReason: 80.lv is a well-established game development trade outlet; excerpt directly and specifically supports the AI-agent collaboration framing with a verbatim Unity design-philosophy quote.

stories.head: Managed Agents gains model-effort control, initial session events and threads delta streaming
stories.brief: Hosted Claude agents get effort tuning, lifecycle session events and delta streams.
stories.tldr: Anthropic’s Python SDK release 0.118.0, dated 2026-07-22, adds API support for Managed Agents model effort, initial session events, and threads delta streaming [1].
stories.why: If you are moving agent orchestration onto Anthropic’s hosted platform, effort control is your cost/latency dial per step and threads delta streaming is what makes a long-running agent observable instead of a black box until it finishes.

sources.claim: Anthropic’s Managed Agents platform gained model-effort control, initial session events, and threads delta streaming on July 22, 2026.
sources.excerpt:

Full Changelog: [v0.117.1...v0.118.0](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/compare/v0.117.1...v0.118.0)

### Features

sources.summary: Anthropic official Python SDK changelog v0.118.0, July 22. Expands the Managed Agents hosted-agent platform with per-agent model-effort tuning, lifecycle session events, and streaming over threads. Same source document as the claude-opus-5 row; different version/date entry.

stories.head: Fab Summer Mega Sale is on — up to 70% off tens of thousands of assets
stories.brief: Epic’s Fab store marks down tens of thousands of assets by as much as 70 percent.
stories.tldr: Epic’s Fab marketplace has opened its Summer Mega Sale, offering up to 70% off tens of thousands of assets [1].
stories.why: A cheap window to stock your UE5 project with materials, meshes and templates — useful if you would rather buy base content and spend your own hours on Nanite and shader work.

sources.claim: Fab marketplace Summer Mega Sale launched July 21 with up to 70% off tens of thousands of assets—including gameplay systems, templates, materials, and character packs—running until 23:59 ET on July 29.
sources.excerpt: Get up to 70% off tens of thousands of assets in the Fab Summer Mega Sale!
sources.summary: Official Unreal Engine news page announcing the Fab Summer Mega Sale. Confirmed published 2026-07-21 via multiple search result cross-references. Page itself is proxy-blocked (403).
sources.trustReason: Official Epic Games/Unreal Engine origin of the claim; excerpt confirms the sale name, 70% off depth, and tens-of-thousands asset volume.

rejected.reason: Third-party anonymous community GitHub repo (47thtechcorner) with no demonstrated affiliation to Moonshot AI; superlative claims (‘world’s first’) are unattributed; the weights-release date (July 27) does not appear in the excerpt at all; cannot verify technical specifications from an unknown aggregator account.

Excerpt is a generic CEO marketing quote (‘Game development is changing faster than ever before in history’) that substantiates none of the claim’s specific technical facts — 90% faster shader builds, zero-rebuild upgrade path, Surface Cache GI, December beta, Q1 2027 release — rendering the claim unverified by the captured evidence regardless of publisher authority.
